clue.text: Pirate on S American river that may be seen on board

definitions.text: that may be seen on board

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate of Treasure Island
the River Plate flows between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is sailing a South American river in a ship you could spot from the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' pulls towards a ship; here the board is a dining table, where plated cutlery and dishes are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver-plated tableware is what you might see laid out on a dining board, an old word for a table.

clue.text: Student involved in chorals

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled or intricate, so the letters of the following word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A student is taking part in choral singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or one holding a scholarship to study, hence a student.

clue.text: Flower some pull up inappropriately

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somebody is uprooting garden flowers when they should not.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden plant with tall spikes of pea-like blooms.

clue.text: Cares a lot about powered flight

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worries a great deal about travelling by aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powered flight' looks like aviation, but the flight is a flight of stairs that moves under its own power.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is a set of steps, or flight, driven by a motor.

clue.text: Past prime minister is the product of sanctimonious island race

parts.note: pi is informal British for smugly pious
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A former premier is said to have been shaped by a self-righteous island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island race' suggests the British people; it is the TT motorbike race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both William Pitt the Elder and the Younger were eighteenth-century heads of British government.

clue.text: The tales bandied about by sportsmen

indicators.note: bandied about means tossed to and fro, so the letters of the phrase are thrown into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Athletes are people who compete in sport, especially track and field events.

clue.text: It may retain warmth that will show at the end of three months

definitions.meaning: a glowing fragment left in a dying fire keeps its heat

definitions.text: that will show at the end of three months
definitions.meaning: the last five letters of the names of September, November and December

explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal fragment holds heat, and the same letters close the names of three autumn and winter months.

clue.text: Mary holding child featured in stonework

indicators.note: holding means one piece wraps round the other, as a mother holds a baby

parts.note: the name is used just as written
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: The Virgin Mary holding the infant Jesus appears in carved stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a nativity carving, but Mary is just her four letters split around SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is building work made of dressed stone or brick.

clue.text: Full make up?

definitions.meaning: full means entire, with nothing lacking
to make up a set or number is to finish it off

explanation.definitionFit: Complete works as the adjective meaning entire and as the verb meaning to finish or round out.

clue.text: Game that's bound to go with whisky

parts.note: to bound is to leap, so hops
Scotch is whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.surface: A game seems tied up with a glass of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' tempts as tied; it is the verb to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Reserves bets on races

definitions.meaning: to reserve a table or seat is to book it
a bookmaker takes or makes ..., records of wagers on races

explanation.definitionFit: Books works as a verb for reserving ahead and as the noun for a bookmaker's record of wagers.

clue.text: Nelly is confused about love, and without boyfriends?

indicators.note: about means the jumbled name goes round the next piece
is confused means jumbled, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Nelly is muddled about romance and has no boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the anagram LNELY of Nelly round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a partner or company may feel isolated and solitary.

clue.text: Reptile brings back one young salmon in ten

indicators.note: in means the reversed salmon and the one go inside the number

parts.note: the number is used as written

indicators.note: brings back means the young fish's name is read in the other direction

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon before it goes to sea
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A reptile returns one young fish in ten.
explanation.walkthrough: A parr is a salmon in its first year or two in fresh water; 'brings back' turns its name round, and 'in' sets it with the one inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, a kind of reptile.

clue.text: Curiosity may make one tarry

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters can be shaped into something new, an anagram

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something unusual might make a person linger.
explanation.definitionFit: A rarity is an uncommon object, the kind of curiosity collectors seek.

clue.text: It takes a turn for the better

definitions.text: It takes a turn for the better

parts.words: It takes a turn for the better
parts.note: a casino wheel spins, taking a turn, for the benefit of a gambler, read as better, one who bets

explanation.definitionFit: The spinning casino wheel is played by gamblers, people who bet on where the ball lands.

clue.text: Dead centre?

parts.note: read as a centre for the dead, a place where they are gathered

explanation.definitionFit: A burial ground is literally the central place where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Place to be for an alibi

definitions.text: Place to be for an alibi

parts.words: Place to be for an alibi
parts.note: an alibi needs the suspect to have been somewhere other than the crime scene

explanation.definitionFit: An alibi proves a suspect was somewhere other than where the crime happened.

clue.text: Chases jobs

explanation.definitionFit: Pursuits covers both acts of hunting or chasing and occupations or hobbies a person follows.

clue.text: Quasar exploding round one high-class constellation

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters surround the next pieces
exploding blows the word apart so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
U is the British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A bright quasar blows up near one select group of stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploding' turns Quasar into AQUARS, which goes 'round' I and U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Water Carrier is a zodiac star group and sign.

clue.text: One more convert on earth

indicators.note: convert means change into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Yet another missionary makes a convert on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one of the same kind.

clue.text: Back on board

parts.note: the rear part of a ship, rather than returning aboard

explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for at or towards the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: This is no way to drink patent medicine

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Swigging alcohol is not the right way to take a branded remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'This is no way' is a reproach; 'no' is just its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a medicine sold with exaggerated claims.

clue.text: Not very bright, so extra-shy

parts.note: over means extra or left in excess
to shy is to throw, so cast

explanation.surface: Someone is rather dim, and also painfully shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid; it is the verb to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast describes a cloudy sky, so a dull, not very bright day.

clue.text: One's saucy prank!

definitions.meaning: a pickled flower bud that goes into sauces such as tartare

explanation.definitionFit: Caper names the pickled bud used in sauces and a frolicking practical joke.

clue.text: Their losses may get roundabout compensation

definitions.text: Their losses may get roundabout compensation

parts.words: Their losses may get roundabout compensation
parts.note: plays on the saying that what you lose on these playground rides you gain on the roundabouts

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'swings and roundabouts' means losses in one place are offset by gains in another; a roundabout here is a playground merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Playground seats hung from chains sit beside merry-go-rounds in the idiom about gains offsetting losses.

clue.text: Chemical, inert in another form

indicators.note: in another form says the letters are reshaped into a new word

parts.note: the word is used as written; that its letters with the following word happen to spell the answer backwards is a coincidence, not the setter's device

explanation.surface: A chemical is unreactive when changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical compound also called saltpetre.

clue.text: One employs American with hesitation

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.walkthrough: 'One employs' is a noun phrase here: one who employs or uses something.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a person who employs or makes use of something.

clue.text: He gets put out, becomes angry

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man is put out and loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed; 'out' is the anagram signal on 'put', making TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is informal for agitated or worked into a temper.

clue.text: Script one created for TV's Morse?

indicators.note: created means the letters are made into something new, an anagram

explanation.surface: A screenplay was written for the television detective Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse is the Oxford detective of the British TV series Inspector Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse holds the police rank of detective chief inspector in the series.

clue.text: Seconds subside?

definitions.meaning: a club's second team is often called the seconds
read as sub side, a side made of substitutes

explanation.definitionFit: A club's second eleven is its backup side, made up of substitutes for the first team.
